stem: In the “cast down your bucket” story, Washington most directly urges his Black audience to

options.text: seek help from Northern philanthropists and the federal government
options.misconception: The bucket means waiting for outside help.

options.text: abandon the South for better opportunities in the West
options.misconception: The bucket means leaving the South.

options.text: build their lives in the South, among their white neighbors
refuse all work until white Southerners grant them equal rights
options.misconception: The bucket means a work stoppage.

rationales.A: The sailors are saved by what is already around them, not by a rescue ship’s charity; the friendly vessel only gives advice.
rationales.B: The story’s point is to stay and draw on what is near, not to sail away.
rationales.C: The thirsty sailors find fresh water by lowering the bucket where they already float. Washington applies the story to his own people: the opportunity is here, in Southern fields, workshops, and trades, among the white neighbors they already live beside.
rationales.D: Washington promises loyalty and devotion, not a work stoppage.
rationales.general:
1. Retell the story. Thirsty sailors find fresh water by lowering the bucket where they are.
2. Ask what the water stands for. Opportunity, already present in the South.
3. Test the other urges. No rescue from outside, no sailing away, no refusal to work.
4. Match the moral. Build your life where you live, among the neighbors you have.
Remember: a parable’s moral is the advice — ask what the story tells its hearers to do.

stimulus.source_note: Booker T. Washington, address at the Atlanta Cotton States and International Exposition, September 18, 1895. Public domain.
stimulus.text:
One-third of the population of the South is of the Negro race. No enterprise seeking the material, civil, or moral welfare of this section can disregard this element of our population and reach the highest success. . . .

A ship lost at sea for many days suddenly sighted a friendly vessel. From the mast of the unfortunate vessel was seen a signal, “Water, water; we die of thirst!” The answer from the friendly vessel at once came back, “Cast down your bucket where you are.” . . .

As we have proved our loyalty to you in the past, in nursing your children, watching by the sick-bed of your mothers and fathers, and often following them with tear-dimmed eyes to their graves, so in the future, in our humble way, we shall stand by you with a devotion that no foreigner can approach, ready to lay down our lives, if need be, in defense of yours; interlacing our industrial, commercial, civil, and religious life with yours in a way that shall make the interests of both races one. In all things that are purely social we can be as separate as the fingers, yet one as the hand in all things essential to mutual progress.

source: original; stimulus is a verbatim public-domain speech
